# The per-module coverage floors of the new core (ADR-0040 item 2), checked by
# .github/scripts/coverage-floor.py: a module below its floor, or a module without a line here, fails
# the job.
#   c   <module> <floor %> <files>   line coverage (llvm-cov) of coretest's tests and vpntest's transport test:
#                                    the coverage job of windows.yml
#   go  <package> <floor %>          statement coverage (go test -coverprofile) of the Linux job of
#                                    ranz.yml, which runs every package of the one Go module
# The mitigation packages (SEC-1 #279) hold Windows-only process mitigation policies, so the Linux jobs
# measure none of their code and their floor is 0.
# A floor is the coverage measured in CI when it was recorded, rounded down to a whole percent, less
# two points for the tests whose paths depend on timing. Raise a floor when a module gains tests; a
# change that lowers one says why in its pull request.

# The new core (src/Core, ADR-0022)
c  corecrypto     85  src/Core/Crypto*.c
c  corenoise      86  src/Core/Noise*.c
# corepeer holds the peer sessions of the data datagrams and the bind challenge (PeerSession.c, PeerChallenge.c;
# CORE-H2 #399), which coretest's peersession, relay, relaypolicy and punch tests run
c  corepeer       72  src/Core/Peer*.c
# coretransport went from 85 to 81 (83.5% measured) when TransportQuic.c joined it (CORE-S1-1 #67): this job
# runs the quic test against msquic, which does not reach the error paths of its dial, backlog and shutdown
c  coretransport  81  src/Core/Transport*.c
# corecontrol (SDN-3 #179) is exercised by vpntest's sdntrace, which needs the controller and rqlite and runs in
# build_and_test, not in this job, so its floor is 0 until this job runs it
c  corecontrol    0  src/Core/Control*.c
# corevxlan (SDN-62 #289) is exercised by vpntest's vxlan test, which this job runs with transport and quic: 88.3%
# measured, less two points for the flood list that changes during a burst from another thread. Its Geneve
# (VxlanGeneve.c, SDN-71 #347) is exercised by vpntest's geneve test, which this job runs with them.
c  corevxlan      86  src/Core/Vxlan*.c
# coreswitch (CORE-S4-1 #74) is exercised by vpntest's switch test, which this job runs with the tests above: 94.6%
# measured, less two points for the threads that forward while ports change and for the random key of the MAC table
c  coreswitch     92  src/Core/Switch*.c
# corepolicy (CORE-S4-2 #75) is exercised by vpntest's policy test, which this job runs with the tests above: 94.0%
# measured, less two points for the threads that judge frames while the documents change
c  corepolicy     92  src/Core/Policy*.c
# corefrontdoor (SDN-29 #205) is exercised by coretest's frontdoor test, whose node and owner processes write their own
# profiles; the node killed in the test writes none
c  corefrontdoor  60  src/Core/FrontDoor*.c
# coresourcelimit (AUD1-DT-3 #451) is exercised by vpntest's sourcelimits test, which this job runs with the tests above: its
# table, its caps, its two token buckets and its sweep; the floor leaves the one out-of-memory path of each allocation
c  coresourcelimit  80  src/Core/SourceLimit*.c

# writes the plans of tests/explain, 87.2% measured at the first run, less two points

# login (SDN-32 #226): the logins of users, which the package's own tests run against a fake controller and a fake token store
# (the conformance of the controller package runs them against the real ones, and counts for that package): 89.3% measured at
# the first run, less two points
go  controller/internal/login           87
# mimic (CORE-P2-1 #85): the Linux job runs the sidecars end to end on Unix sockets, with the REALITY
# library, uTLS and an ACME service of the test; pipe_windows.go is the part that only Windows builds.
# 91.6% was measured in the first run, in which the tests that move a stream failed, so it is a lower
# bound: the floor is that less two points for the tests whose paths depend on timing, and it is to be
# raised to the measure of a run in which they pass
go  controller/internal/mimic           89
go  controller/internal/mitigation      0
# nodecontroller (SDN-90 #395): the Controller settings of a Node, every path tested on every OS but
# the key of settings that Parse did not return; the floor is set below the measure until a run records it
go  controller/internal/nodecontroller  90
go  controller/internal/nodesim         0
# password (SDN-31 #225): the Linux job measures password.go and pbkdf2_other.go; the CNG derivation of pbkdf2_windows.go
# is the Windows job's, which checks it against the standard library: 93.0% measured, less two points
go  controller/internal/password        91
# payload (ONE-2 #311) has real logic tested on every OS (payload_test.go: the hash checks, the
